items.title: If the outage had been worse, would the same treatment still read as honest?
items.description: Draft B names its outage in one clause — about 31% of the draft's word count — and that reads as honest framing for the 12-minute outage it actually describes. Drag the outage's length toward the 4-hour, paying-customers version L3's closing question asks you to imagine, while the treatment stays exactly the same size. The gap that opens up is the space a more serious fact would have deserved but didn't get — which is what starts to read as spin to an outside reader, even though every sentence stays factual.

params.name: outageMinutes
params.label: How long the outage actually lasted

items.compute: const actualSharePercent = 31; const baselineMinutes = 12; const maxMinutes = 240; const ratio = (params.outageMinutes - baselineMinutes) / (maxMinutes - baselineMinutes); const spinGap = Math.round(64 * Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, ratio))); return { spinGap };

outputs.label: How much the unchanged, brief mention now reads as spin
